question: A sector of a circle having a radius of 10 cm and has a central angle of (3pi)/(4) radians. What is the area of the sector?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the angle θ is given in radians, the formula for the area of a sector is: Area = 1/2 × r² × θ

Area = 1/2 × 10² × (3π ÷ 4)

Area = 50 × 0.75π = 37.5π cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 37.5π cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 3π/4 rad 10 cm 10 cm O 

**Given:**

Radius of the circle (r) = 10 cm

Central angle (θ) = 3π ÷ 4 radians

**Formula Used:**

Area of a sector = 1/2 × r² × θ (where θ is measured in radians)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area = 1/2 × (10)² × (3π ÷ 4)

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 100 × (3π ÷ 4)

⇒ Area = 50 × (3π ÷ 4)

⇒ Area = 150π ÷ 4

⇒ Area = 37.5π cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 37.5π cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Sector (Degree Measure)

If the central angle is given in degrees instead of radians, the formula changes to: Area = (θ ÷ 360) × πr².

Length of an Arc

The curved boundary length of the sector (Arc Length, L) is calculated using L = r × θ (when θ is in radians).

Perimeter of a Sector

The total boundary length of a sector can be found by adding the arc length and both radii: P = L + 2r.
